1.explanation:
• language-support.md – shows how Prettier parses Markdown and raw HTML blocks, which is directly relevant to understanding why HTML inside lists is treated specially.  
• options.md – documents Prettier options (e.g. tabWidth, htmlWhitespaceSensitivity, parser) that control HTML formatting behavior and indentation.  
• configuration.md – explains how to set up a .prettierrc or other config file to tweak Markdown and HTML format rules, so you can reproduce or override default indent settings.  
• editors.md – details editor integrations (including VS Code) and how the format-on-save feature is wired up, which is the trigger for the bug.  
• technical-details.md – delves into Prettier’s AST generation and printer logic, helping debug why nested HTML in lists gets cumulatively indented.  
• ignore.md – shows how to exclude files or patterns if you want to temporarily avoid formatting Markdown, a common workaround mentioned in the report.
1.bug_scenario: In VS Code with Prettier’s “format on save” enabled, a Markdown file that contains nested raw HTML (an HTML <table> under a numbered list) is repeatedly re-indented by one extra level each time you save. The attached GIF shows a markdown list item (“1. Some test text…”) wrapping a <table> block. On first save Prettier indents the <tr> rows one level too deep; on subsequent saves it continually adds more leading spaces, pushing the table further out of alignment. The key elements are the Markdown ordered list marker, the raw HTML block inside it, VS Code’s format-on-save hook invoking Prettier, and Prettier’s Markdown/HTML indentation logic.
